title: CoordinateGermConcentrationData
statement: In the finite setting [def-pur-conventions], use the affine spaces [def-sbc-affine-space], support kernels and normalized germs [def-pur-etale-coordinate-support], supported coefficients [def-pur-supported-exterior-product], ordinary signed cup classes and comparison [def-pur-supported-class-operations] and comparison [def-pur-supported-hom-site-comparison], and the ordered frame boundary product [def-pur-frame-class]. For b≥0, define N=A^b_k and its coordinate zero subscheme. Let L_s=A(s)(k), K_r=RΓ_0(N,A(r)), and let D(i,t,r) be the bounded-below derived supported stalk. The ordered ordinary class c_N is the unique ordinary supported class whose canonical comparison is the ordered frame boundary product (including the empty unit). For every v in L_(r-b), form c_N tensor v with the prescribed signed cup multiplication, using the actual global coefficient section determined by v. The support-coefficient adjunction to the literal global restriction kernel is the unique adjunction whose inverse Hom equivalence followed by the closed coefficient quotient is the ordinary constant-sheaf adjoint followed by inclusion of the kernel. Use this uniquely normalized adjunction, not an arbitrary one. The coefficient pullback, field-to-supported-stalk germ and single sheaves are those of the recorded support and signed-twist constructions. Use the shared localization, equality reindexing and identity-support unitor of [def-pur-supported-class-normalizations].
